title: Constant strict towers and normalized derived direct image

source.place: Proof Step 5, proper/direct-image generator and final normalization paragraph

proof.text: Retain the established construction of the derived reduction model from K-flat resolutions and its universal counit. Construct the ordinary tensor unit with the existing normalized scalar-extension adjunction. Its section formula is x ↦ 1 tensor x. Construct quotient transitions by the same adjunction, restricting their targets along the quotient factor map. Linearity and the tensor-unit formula give s tensor x ↦ q(s) tensor x. The tensor-section extensionality lemma proves naturality and uniqueness of transitions and of the whole-tower augmentation.

For an ordinary module pullback, the square of scalar restrictions and pullback is invertible. Its mate under the two scalar-extension adjunctions is invertible: transpose it once more under geometric pullback/direct-image adjunctions, where it is the invertible restriction/direct-image comparison. The unit equation for this mate gives the formula on 1 tensor x. Linearity gives the formula on every local pure tensor. Naturality of constant coefficient pullback with respect to quotient factor maps proves compatibility with all tower transitions. These component isomorphisms assemble to ordinaryReductionPull; tensor-section extensionality after the geometric adjunction proves its required uniqueness.

Use an inverse-image-adapted flat resolution: the source complex is K-flat and its exact pullback is K-flat. Identify the given constant-coefficient pullback with the algebraic inverse image followed by coefficient transport. On this resolving class both derived-reduction counits compute the ordinary reduction. Compare the two derived composites by restriction along the resolving-class localization, using the ordinary whole-tower isomorphism and exact-localization factors. The fully faithful restriction yields an isomorphism, its displayed representative equation, and uniqueness. This proves reductionPull_existsUnique without adding an intermediate hole.

Keep the canonical right-derived composite comparison defining chi. The four universal-unit equations of its constituent isomorphisms give its formula on every homotopy object. On a K-injective representative the right-derived units are the inverse computation isomorphisms, giving exactly IsDirectImageNormalizedOnKInjectives. Comparing universal derived units also identifies chi with the derived adjunction mate of the constant/pullback square; the ordinary mate is the identity-component constant/direct-image square by the adjunction triangle identity.

Exact derived squares respect composition. Apply this to the constant-tower and evaluation squares, whose ordinary components are identities; the identity-functor coherence equations give the constant/evaluation normalization for deltaPull. Mates preserve composition, so transposing that equation gives precisely the required identity involving chi, the specified evalR, and deltaEval. For inverse limit, transpose the same square once more along the diagonal/limit adjunctions. Its unit equation and the invertibility of the diagonal units cancel chi with its inverse and give the displayed identity involving limitPush and deltaLimit.

The ordinary quotient augmentation commutes with ordinaryReductionPull: transpose under geometric pullback and check its sections, where the defining formulas on 1 tensor x agree and the coefficient map preserves one. Pass this square to homotopy categories degreewise. The universal left-derived lift defining augmentation has the same counit factorization as the ordinary augmentation. On inverse-image-adapted K-flat representatives, the representative equation for reductionPull and these two factorizations prove the derived augmentation square after cancellation of the computing counit. Resolving quasi-isomorphisms extend the equality to every derived object. Finally naturality of the adjunction-mates correspondence in the two vertical functors transposes this square into the required projection/augmentation equation, with chi identified by its already-proved mate formula.

split_report.summary: Expanded the constant-tower direct-image normalization into four steps. The split constructs the diagonal derived direct-image isomorphism on the diagram site, checks its evaluation and derived-limit normalization on K-injective representatives, constructs the quotient-tower projection mate by the ringed-site counit-tensor formula, and proves the augmentation equation by its unit normalization. No new DAG nodes were needed. Generic direct-image/limit comparison is used for the canonical map a and its underived normalization on a diagonal tower.
Generic ringed-topos projection mate supplies the counit-tensor map, naturality, and tensor-unit normalization used to define h and prove clause (4).
Generic derived tensor/pullback comparison identifies the diagram-site tensor used in the projection mate with the specified reduction tower.
Generic K-injective preservation by a right adjoint to an exact functor justifies the diagonal K-injective representative.
Generic existence of K-injective resolutions is used to choose the representative for the unbounded derived direct image.
Generic total-derived-functor computation on K-injectives identifies the literal diagonal direct image with R_f^T.
Generic K-flat resolution is used to realize the quotient tensor tower strictly before localization.
Generic exact inverse image for arbitrary constant rings identifies coefficient pullbacks and makes direct image preserve K-injectives; finite-ring specializations do not cover A.

lean.statement: theorem constantTowerDirectImageNormalization (d : CompleteCoefficientDatum A) {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) : IsDirectImageNormalizedOnKInjectives (moduleDirectImage A f) (Functor.const ℕᵒᵖ : Modules A X ⥤ Towers A X) (Functor.const ℕᵒᵖ : Modules A Y ⥤ Towers A Y) (towerDirectImage A f) (Functor.compConstIso ℕᵒᵖ (moduleDirectImage A f)) (chi A f) ∧ (∀ (M : DerivedCategory (Modules A X)) (n : ℕ), (ev A Y n).map ((chi A f).hom.app M) ≫ (evalR A f n).app ((delta A X).obj M) ≫ (push A f).map ((deltaEval A X n).hom.app M) = (deltaEval A Y n).hom.app ((push A f).obj M)) ∧ (∀ M : DerivedCategory (Modules A X), (push A f).map ((deltaLimit A X).inv.app M) ≫ (limitPush A f).hom.app ((delta A X).obj M) ≫ (L A Y).map ((chi A f).inv.app M) ≫ (deltaLimit A Y).hom.app ((push A f).obj M) = 𝟙 _) ∧ (∀ M : DerivedCategory (Modules A X), (augmentation d.ideal Y).app ((push A f).obj M) ≫ (projection d.ideal f).app M = (chi A f).hom.app M ≫ (R A f).map ((augmentation d.ideal X).app M))
